sections.content:
35,560 people

were counted on the census as "housing officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Housing officers assess and address housing needs of particular localities and individuals and oversee the day-to-day management of rented properties belonging to local authorities or housing associations.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "housing officers", 14.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "housing officers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "housing officers" included:

  • welfare professionals (other)
  • credit controllers
  • public services associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "housing officers" there were more women than men (69.9% compared with 30.1%).

This means "housing officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 30.1% and women made up 69.9% of "housing officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "housing officers" included:

  • dispensing opticians
  • coffee shop workers
  • human resources and industrial relations officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "housing officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "housing officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "housing officers", 15.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.2% compared with 19.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.6%) than self-employed (2.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
